Page 46 of 54 DE-EE0009512 Massachusetts Institute of Technology Project 8: Device Stability and Lifetime Correlation Under Different Stressors and Environments This section relates to our studies on how the device stability is affected by different stressors (humidity, temperature, and light intensity), and to determine the correlation between the stress condition and device lifetime. Encouraged by the promising stability results discussed in Project 5 above, all devices now reported in this section are based on our new simplified spiro- MeOTAD hole-transporting layer. In terms of thermal stability, we heated our unencapsulated devices at different temperatures of 25°C, 45°C, 65°C, and 85°C inside a nitrogen glovebox. Periodically before each I-V measurement, the devices would be cooled first at room temperature in the glovebox. Figure 8.1a plots the average PCEs (absolute values) of 4 devices each at the different temperatures except for 85°C (2 best devices). No obvious degradation was observed for over 500 hours for the devices heated at 25°C, 45°C, and 65°C. On average, only the devices aged at 85 °C showed noticeable degradation.
